rfp_requirements.title: Acknowledge Order of Precedence of Contractual Terms
rfp_requirements.description: Bidder must recognize that in the event of a conflict among the Contract documents, the stated order of precedence from highest to lowest ranking applies.

rfp_requirements.title: Acknowledge State Tax Set-Off
rfp_requirements.description: Contractor acknowledges that pursuant to N.J.S.A. 54:49-19, whenever the Contractor (or a partner/shareholder) is entitled to payment while indebted for any State tax, the Director of the Division of Taxation shall seek to set off that amount.

rfp_requirements.title: Designate Project Manager and backup
rfp_requirements.description: Identify and provide a designated Project Manager (PM) and no less than one (1) backup personnel authorized to act as PM to support and communicate with the SCM as requested or required.

rfp_requirements.title: Include acronyms/terms appendix in BC/DR plan
Address participant roles in BC/DR plan
Address stakeholder roles in BC/DR plan
Include acronyms/terms appendix in backup plan
Retain offsite backups for no less than one year
Require authorization to use mobile devices
rfp_requirements.description: Establish requirements for authorization to use mobile devices for organizational business purposes.

rfp_requirements.title: Notice to Division of Law before defending in State's name
rfp_requirements.description: Neither Contractor nor its attorney shall defend a claim in the name of the State or any Authorized Purchaser, or act as its legal representative, without providing notice to the Director of the Division of Law and the Director of the Division of Purchase and Property.

rfp_requirements.title: Notify Division of Law before defending in State's name
rfp_requirements.description: Neither Contractor nor any attorney engaged by Contractor may defend the claim in the name of the State or purport to act as legal representative without providing notice to the Director of the Division of Law and Director of Division of Purchase and Property.

rfp_requirements.title: Grant Union representative reasonable access
rfp_requirements.description: A representative of the Union shall have reasonable access to the Employer for the purpose of conferring with the Employer, shop stewards, and Employees and for administering this Agreement.

rfp_requirements.title: Provide Bulletin Board at each location
rfp_requirements.description: The Employer shall provide a Bulletin Board at each location, placed conspicuously and readily accessible, to be used for posting proper Union notices.

rfp_requirements.title: Limit emergency/personal sick leave use
rfp_requirements.description: Full-time employees may use no more than 40 hours per year and part-time employees no more than 20 hours per year of sick leave for emergency or personal reasons.

rfp_requirements.title: Limit partial-day sick leave to specified purposes
rfp_requirements.description: Sick leave for less than a full work day may only be used for onset of illness while working, tending to an ill immediate family member, or medical appointments that could not be arranged during non-work time.

rfp_requirements.title: State officer/employee bids subject to Attorney General conflict-of-interest guidelines
rfp_requirements.description: Any State officer, employee, or group of State officers/employees entering into a contract as a private contractor under this section must do so subject to guidelines for conflict of interest established by the Attorney General.

I-5F: Disaster Recovery
Disaster prevention and recovery is a mainstay of Parsons’ IT systems and operations methods and we have consistently
maintained a reliable network and mitigated risks through our disaster recovery approach. Our primary goal in disaster
recovery (DR) is to manage the event to reduce its impact and ensure continuous delivery of the PA I/M Program. We
activ

ure the recovery of system operations during a disaster which disrupts the online
VIID capabilities or interrupts operational delivery of the Program. By designing a fault-tolerant system that offers
automatic and immediate recovery for most disaster scenarios, Parsons enables the VIID to continue its operation
uninterrupted. We’ll host our updated system environment in the Amazon Web Service (AWS) US-EAST-1 region to take
advantage of the isolated data center locations, called availability zones, which exceed the 99% service level requirement
for availability and uptime of all systems applications. Our disaster recovery strategy also includes redundancy distributed
across two availability zones to ensure maximized protection with the capacity to take over complete production volume
in each availability zone and provide a responsive end-user experience even in disaster scenarios. Each availability zone
is engineered to be isolated from failures in other availability zones and provides fault tolerance and low-latency network
connectivity to other availability zones in the same region. We’ve evaluated the data center locations for multiple risks,
including flood and other environment

available to end-users.
Our proven applications run in all our programs, and we provide unmatched uptime results. “Exhibit I-5-1” shows the
uptime percentages for our VIID solutions in our programs.

I-5G: Back-Up and Back-Up Storage
Parsons has established procedures for backup of all data and application files. Our experience in other programs with
retrieval and recovery of data and application files is reflected in the careful development of the back-up plan for the PA
I/M Program. PennDOT has approved our procedures, minimizing concern and transition risk to the Commonwealth upon
transition to the new contract. The backup plan includes:
§ Daily real-time full and incremental application files and data backups
§ Instant backup and recovery of data from snapshots
§ Configuration management system and application code stored in version control system, included in daily backup
To protect against data corruption, and to p

n, and to provide the ability to restore point-in-time, Parsons performs full and
incremental VIID data backups daily in real-time using specialized archiving software and snapshots. This affords the
flexibility to instantly create a copy, restore full or partial data, and restore data from snapshots, which is non-disruptive
and much faster than traditional backup sources. The database management tools include the capability of logging and
journalizing each backup. Parsons’ use of snapshot technology minimizes impact on the database environment when the
backup process is invoked.
In addition, cross-availability zone and cross-region data replication and specific data backup retention levels protect
against data corruption, data loss, and major disasters. We will use AWS Aurora database and S3 object storage to store
critical PA I/M Program data, allowing data to be replicated across multiple availability zones. In addition, we will use AWS
backup service to automate data backups and replication to an alternate region, ensuring multiple copies of the Program
data exist in geographically dispersed areas at any given time and exceeding redundancy requirements.

of the COVID-19 pandemic, supporting contractual deliverables while prioritizing employee safety. Our ability to maintain
operations comes in part from our established Emergency Response Plan (described below) and our experienced
Program Management Team.

communications, and data transfer capabilities. As proven during the COVID-19 pandemic, our entire project team,
including management, office, call center, and field staff, are equipped to work remotely, enabling continuation of critical
business services without facility access.
If a particular region is affected by an emergency, operations can be directed to any of the remaining operational regions.
All management, office, and quality assurance personnel can support operations in other regions and continue providing
essential business activities. Quality assurance personnel can be productive in any area of the state, allowing for
coverage if some staff members are unavailable due to emergency conditions.

will forward telephone numbers to unaffected regional offices to ensure station and consumer issues are addressed. All
regional Program information is stored remotely, preventing loss and allowing access by other regional and remote
project staff during unplanned office closures.
If an emergency impacts a VIID hosting location or VIID functionality, the Disaster Recovery Plan (referenced in I-5G
above and Attachment B) will be implemented to minimize or avoid disruption of critical business functions.
If an emergency impacts the stations’ ability to connect to the VIID, our systems will be able to continue testing for 30
days or 100 inspections, as per the offline test limits set by the VIID and determined by PennDOT. Allowing offline testing
minimizes negative impacts to both the inspection industry and the public. Once connectivity is restored, any offline
testing will automatically upload to the VIID.
